verdict.rationale: Teller documents registrable outbound webhooks: you configure a URL in the Teller Dashboard, and Teller calls it when changes are detected in user enrollments or their financial data. That covers the core push model and plausibly connection-state and data changes. However, the evidence shows no signature verification and no enumerated event types for new transactions or balance updates. Missing for 10: documented webhook signing/verification, explicit event types for new transactions, balance updates and connection state changes, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, data changes arrive as signed webhooks — new transactions, balance updates, connection state changes — so my system stays current without polling

citations.quote: To register a new webhook, you need to have a URL in your app that Teller can call. You can configure a new webhook from the Teller Dashboard
Teller sends webhook events when specific conditions or changes are detected in user enrollments or their financial data.
